gap: No result ChatGPT got that I opened states MonsGeek's own switch rule for the FUN60 Ultra TMR: it reads downward-facing N-pole magnets only, Akko's Creamy Yellow magnetic switch (S-pole) is excluded by name, and only the six switches listed in the MonsGeek driver are guaranteed 0.01 mm precision while others may run at 0.1 mm.
standout_why: Compared against the pages I opened: MKB Guide (says only 'compatible magnetic switches' and 'selected 5-pin MX', and already has the HE65 V2 TMR's 8,000 Hz USB/2.4 GHz and 125 Hz Bluetooth), PCWorld (5-pin mixing only), Notebookcheck (hot-swap, recalibrate, 8K wired and 2.4 GHz), keyboardtester.click (hot-swap one-liners, no Bluetooth figure for the TK75 TMR or FUN60), HLPlanet's TMR-vs-HE page (says magnet polarity is not discussed) and RTINGS' 60% list (name only). None names an excluded switch, a polarity, or the 0.01 mm vs 0.1 mm split. Not opened, so not ruled out: TechRadar, both GamePadSquire pages, RTINGS' under-$100 list, RigGrade, Newegg Insider, apidog, deal.ai.
decides: It confirms the picks rather than changing them. A buyer who plans to swap magnetic switches gets a maker-published rule only from MonsGeek (N-pole, six driver-listed switches at 0.01 mm, others 0.1 mm); I could not open a named list from Epomaker or Gamakay. For multi-device use, the Gamakay TK75 TMR keeps 1,000 Hz on Bluetooth (HLPlanet's spec table) against 125 Hz on the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR (APH Networks' copy of the maker table). Ours honestly wins the 75% segment: it was the only 75% TMR board at or under $100 on the makers' stores I read today, and only at the sale price. MonsGeek's FUN60 Ultra TMR page also carries pre-order, waitlist and 'Unavailable' notices, so its $79.99-$89.99 needs a stock check before it is quoted.

findings.label: Magnet polarity the board reads, and the switch MonsGeek excludes by name
findings.value: Downward-facing N-pole magnetic switches; Akko Magnetic Creamy Yellow (downward-facing S-pole) is 'not compatible with the FUN60'
findings.source_title: FUN60 Ultra TMR product page - MonsGeek
findings.note: Maker's product page. MonsGeek's knowledge base repeats 'downward-facing N-pole magnetic switches' for the FUN60 family.

findings.label: Precision with third-party magnetic switches
findings.value: Six switches listed in the MonsGeek driver (including Akko Glare) guaranteed 0.01 mm; 'other switches may perform at 0.1mm precision'
findings.source_title: FUN60 Ultra TMR product page - MonsGeek
findings.note: The page says 'cross-compatibility with 5 third-party magnetic switches' but does not name them; they are chosen from a list in the driver. MonsGeek says to calibrate in the driver after a swap.

findings.label: Mechanical switch support
findings.value: 'Hot-swappable with 5-Pin Mechanical Switches (MagMech Compatible, TMR Version only)'
findings.source_title: FUN60 Ultra TMR product page - MonsGeek
findings.note: MonsGeek's knowledge base (updated 30/9/2025) instead says the FUN60 Ultra TMR takes any 3-pin or 5-pin mechanical switch, and that FUN60 Pro and Max take none. The two maker pages differ on 3-pin.

findings.label: Gateron magnetic switches, as MonsGeek's knowledge base states it
findings.value: Reversed-polarity Gateron switches 'doesn't work on our PCB at the moment (as of Feb, 2024)'
findings.note: The line is dated Feb 2024 and is not tied to a named board, so it may predate the FUN60. Check the driver list before using it as a FUN60 exclusion.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection, maker
findings.value: 8,000 Hz wired or 2.4 GHz; no Bluetooth figure given (Bluetooth 5.0, 3 devices)
findings.source_title: FUN60 Ultra TMR product page - MonsGeek
findings.note: Rapid trigger 0.01 mm. Actuation 0.1-3.4 mm on web.monsgeek.com, 0.1-3.3 mm on app.monsgeek.com. 4,000 mAh on tri-mode. No operating system list on the page.

findings.label: Driver and connection limits Notebookcheck found
findings.value: Desktop driver 'couldn't initialize in the 2.4 GHz mode' (worked wired and on Bluetooth); driver cannot change the polling rate; about 3 h on 2.4 GHz with LEDs on
findings.source_title: MonsGeek Fun60 Ultra TMR hands-on review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: Notebookcheck review dated 2025-03-30. It says Bluetooth does not reach 8 kHz but gives no figure. It quotes $79.99 wired, $89.99 tri-mode.

findings.label: Price and availability on MonsGeek's US page
findings.value: $79.99-$89.99 (USB-C wired or tri-mode); page shows pre-order ('will not ship instantly'), waitlist and 'Unavailable' notices
findings.source_title: FUN60 Ultra TMR product page - MonsGeek
findings.note: The page does not tie the notices or the two prices to a specific colour or connection variant; select each variant before quoting. PCWorld's review (read today) gives MonsGeek's listed price as $74.99.

findings.label: Price, Epomaker US store
findings.note: Read through the store's search endpoint with storecheck.py; the product page itself returned HTTP 429, so variants and any dispatch notice were not read.

findings.label: Switch and device support, maker's listing text
findings.value: Hybrid hot-swap: magnetic switches and standard 3/5-pin mechanical switches; 'full support for Mac, Android, and iOS'
findings.note: Listing text from the store's search endpoint. It names no compatible third-party magnetic switch and no exclusion.

findings.label: Polling rate and latency by connection (maker spec table as APH Networks reproduces it)
findings.value: 8,000 Hz USB and 2.4 GHz, 125 Hz Bluetooth; latency 0.125 ms wired/2.4 GHz, 14 ms Bluetooth
findings.source_title: Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR Review - APH Networks
findings.note: Jadon Lee, APH Networks, 2026-09-18. Same table: 65% ANSI US only, 66 keys + knob, 4,000 mAh, EPOMAKER V4 software, compatibility Mac/WIN/Android. MKB Guide already states the 8,000/125 Hz split.

findings.label: Price, Gamakay US store
findings.source_title: GamaKay TK75 TMR 75% Mechanical Keyboard - 8K Polling Rate, Magnetic Switch
findings.note: Read through the store's search endpoint with storecheck.py; the product page returned HTTP 429 on five tries. keyboardtester.click listed it at $109.99 sale on 2026-11-05, so it is under $100 only at the current sale price.

findings.label: Polling rate by connection (HLPlanet spec table)
findings.value: 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz; 1,000 Hz Bluetooth
findings.note: Marcus Richardson, HLPlanet, 2026-05-18. Same table: Windows and Mac; ANSI US (81 keys) and ISO DE (82 keys). 8 times the HE65 V2 TMR's 125 Hz Bluetooth figure.

findings.label: Mechanical switch support and its limit (HLPlanet)
findings.value: Accepts 5-pin mechanical switches; rapid trigger should be turned off on any key fitted with a mechanical switch or it can double-click
findings.note: Marcus Richardson also reports misread releases on neighbouring keys below about 0.3 mm rapid-trigger sensitivity and recommends about 0.4 mm.

findings.label: Software (HLPlanet)
findings.value: Web app, Gear Hub/Lab at gearhub.top
findings.note: Reviewer's statement; Gamakay's own page was not readable today.

findings.label: Gamakay switch generation the maker restricts
findings.value: V1 Mercury and Phoenix magnetic switches 'only work for the TK75HE V1'
findings.source_title: Gamakay Hall Effect v1 Magnetic Switches
findings.note: Listing text from the store's search endpoint. It means the V1 switch pack ($3.99 and up) is not a spare for the TK75 TMR, which ships with V3 Phoenix or Mercury.

findings.source_title: Womier K75 TMR 75% Wireless Magnetic Gaming Keyboard
findings.note: Store search endpoint. Womier's spec list: tri-mode, magnetic and mechanical switches, 6,000 mAh (2 x 3,000), web driver and desktop software. It gives no polling rate per mode.

findings.label: Price, Womier store (over the line)
findings.source_title: Womier SK75 TMR Wireless Magnetic Switch Aluminum Keyboard
findings.note: Store search endpoint. Womier says 'compatible with mechanical and most magnetic switch brands', actuation 0.1-3.5 mm, 8,000 mAh, online driver.

findings.label: Price, Epomaker US store (just over the line)
findings.note: Store search endpoint. With the two Womier boards over $100, the TK75 TMR at $89.99 was the only 75% TMR board at or under $100 on the maker stores read today.
